sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:46

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 9:46:1
items.html:
And comprehended the dust of the earth in a Shalish [third-measure], for the measure of the earth, which is Malchut, was a third of the Yesod, which is the measure of the Atara [crown]: There is great depth in these words, and a great need to understand them. The matter is that you already know that because of the rising of the bottom Hey to the Einayim, the AHP went out from all the degrees, outside of them. Thus, in each degree, only three Sefirot remained, namely Keter, Hochma, and GAR of Bina. For the ZA of Bina, and ZA and Nukva, went out from her and fell to the lower degree, as is known. This is the secret of the division of every Sefira into three thirds: Keter, Hochma, Bina. And the whole Gadlut of them is only Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama — Neshama in Keter, Ruach in Hochma, and Nefesh in Bina. For with ZA and Malchut of the vessels missing, Keter and Hochma of the lights are missing, as is known from the inverse relation between the vessels and the lights. And you already know that the matter of the rising of the bottom Hey in the Einayim is the secret of the partnership of the quality of mercy in judgment, whose beginning came out in the world of Nekudim, but it was not sustained because of the event of the breaking of the vessels; rather, the beginning of its persistence starts from the world of correction onward, namely from the world of Atzilut, as is known.
Now, these three thirds mentioned in every Sefira underwent a great change in the Sefira of Yesod. This is because Bina’s expansion reaches only until Hod, as is written in The Zohar. The reason for this has already been clarified: it is because of the lack of Hassadim in the vessel of Yesod, as above (page 336, the passage beginning “In a manner.” Study it there well), for only the posterior light of Hod reached the vessel of Yesod, because of the refinement of phase one, which is the level of the five Hassadim; therefore that vessel became there a root for the five Gevurot. See there. And although this was in the Partzuf of AB of AK, still there the vessels received their first form; for in the Partzuf of Keter of AK, the vessels and the lights were mixed with one another, without any distinguishing feature at all to discern between them, as is written there, and in Part Four. This is the secret that Bina ends in the Sefira of Hod, for there the coarseness of phase one was refined, and the level of Hassadim — which is the discernment of Bina, which is nothing but the light of Hassadim, as is known — was nullified. And you see that in the vessel of Yesod there are only two vessels, Keter and Hochma, and the vessel of Bina is missing there; thus the vessel of Yesod, compared to the other vessels, is missing its lower third.
Therefore, at the time the bottom Hey rose in the Einayim, Bina received into herself the restriction of Malchut, and Malchut received into herself the quality of mercy of Bina, in the secret of “and they both went.” Until Hochma herself divided and was corrected into male and female, as is written in The Zohar that Aba brought Ima outside for the sake of her son, and Aba himself was corrected in the likeness of male and female. This is the secret of the Nikvey Einayim, for the Einayim, which are Hochma, were corrected in the Nukva, as mentioned above. Then the bottom Hey rose and was incorporated in the Yesod, and became its lower third, in the secret of “a crown to the head of the righteous.” And then the Yesod attained three levels, like the other Sefirot — except that there is still a great difference between them: for in all the Sefirot, their lower third is the discernment of the vessel of Bina, namely GAR of Bina, as above. But in the Yesod, its lower third is found in the discernment of the bottom Hey, which is Malchut after she joined with Bina and received from her the quality of mercy. And understand that there is an immense difference between the lower third of the other Sefirot, which is the discernment of Bina herself, who received the discernment of the bottom Hey into herself in order to be sweetened, and the lower third of the Yesod, which is the bottom Hey herself, but has in her the sweetening of Bina in the secret of the aforementioned joining.
By this you will understand the secret of the verse, “and comprehended the dust of the earth in a Shalish,” which the ARI interprets as referring to the vessel of the Yesod: its lower third, which is the Atara, is called “the dust of the earth,” which is Malchut, etc. And by this he teaches us that the lower third of the Yesod is not like the other vessels, which is Bina, but is Malchut herself, for she acquired her place there, and there is her root.
There is a further understanding needed here. According to the known rule, the way of the vessels is that the upper ones grow first — the opposite of the lights, in which the lower ones grow first. If so, it is difficult: there is no discernment of Malchut at all in the ten Sefirot, since after the rising of the bottom Hey in the Einayim, in no Partzuf or Sefira remain more than three vessels alone, which are Keter, Hochma, Bina, and in the lights, Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama. If so, how is it possible for Malchut to receive her correction at a time when she has no existence in any Sefira? This is what the ARI teaches us: that she has an existence remaining in the lower third of the Yesod, for the Yesod, by its root, has no portion in Bina, as above; therefore it took the bottom Hey in her place, as written above.
